groups.label: AudioLink Response
groups.info: Master switch for AudioLink on this material, and how sharply reactions decay. Matches the main shader, so an eye and the bodywork set to the same band respond identically.

groups.label: AudioLink Settings
groups.info: Makes the eye's glow react to AudioLink, using the same bands and chain as the main shader so an eye can be matched to bodywork.

groups.label: Light Based
groups.info: Dims or lifts the glow by how lit the eye is, so it can fade in daylight or only show in the dark.

groups.label: Scan / Sweep
groups.info: A bright band that sweeps across the glow, matching the main shader's sweep so an eye can be synced to bodywork.

groups.label: LTCGI
groups.info: Enables LTCGI area light support, so the avatar picks up coloured light from LTCGI world screens and emitters.

groups.label: VRSL GI
groups.info: Lighting from VRSL GI stage rigs - club and event rig fixtures light the eyes, cones respected. No package to install: the world publishes the data as a global, so it switches itself on in VRSL GI worlds and costs nothing elsewhere. Cannot be previewed in the editor.

groups.label: Debug Views
groups.info: Renders one isolated term instead of the finished eye. Set back to Off before locking: it drives an //ifex, so Off strips the feature from the locked shader and anything else ships the debug view to everyone.

tooltips.name: _EyeWrapLight
tooltips.text: Diagnostic aid, off by default. Switches diffuse to half-lambert (wrapped) so the eye still catches light even when the eyeball mesh has inverted or inward-facing normals - the usual cause of an eye that renders black while the face beside it is lit. Turn it on if you hit that, but it softens the terminator and flattens the eye, so fixing the normals is the better fix where you can.

tooltips.name: _PackMode
tooltips.text: How to read the Packed Map. ZFS Packed uses R=Metallic, G=AO, B=Smoothness. Unity MetallicSmoothness (the format most prepacked eye maps ship in) uses R=Metallic and Alpha=Smoothness, with no AO channel - pick this if your eyes render black with a prepacked map.

tooltips.name: _PackedMap
tooltips.text: Metallic/AO/Smoothness. See Packed Map Format above for channel layout. Unassigned defaults to white; if that blacks out the eye, your map is Unity MetallicSmoothness format - switch the format above.

tooltips.name: _SpecStrength
tooltips.text: Brightness of the direct specular highlight in Realistic PBR mode. Gives a plain eye a catchlight with no extra toggles. Ignored in Toon mode.

tooltips.name: _ReflFlipX
tooltips.text: Mirror the reflected environment left-right. Off is correct for a standard eye mesh; enable only if a world's probe reads mirrored horizontally.

tooltips.name: _ReflFlipY
tooltips.text: Mirror the reflected environment up-down. ON by default: a convex eye samples the cubemap Y-inverted, so this puts the sky up and the ground down. Turn off only to see the raw sample.

tooltips.name: _StyleSpecUseLight
tooltips.text: Multiply the glint by the scene light colour, so it dims in dark rooms instead of glowing white. Turn off only for a stylised glint that ignores world lighting.

tooltips.name: _LTCGI
tooltips.text: Enables LTCGI area light support and sets the LTCGI shader keyword. Needs the LTCGI package in the project.

tooltips.name: _LTCGIStrength
tooltips.text: How strongly LTCGI area lights affect the avatar.

tooltips.name: _LTCGITintOn
tooltips.text: Multiply LTCGI diffuse and specular by a colour, to warm or cool the light from world screens.

tooltips.name: _LTCGIDiffuseTint
tooltips.text: Colour multiplied into the LTCGI diffuse contribution.

tooltips.name: _LTCGISpecularTint
tooltips.text: Colour multiplied into the LTCGI specular contribution.

tooltips.name: _LTCGIOcclusion
tooltips.text: How strongly baked AO darkens LTCGI. 0 ignores AO (screens light crevices freely), 1 applies it fully.

tooltips.name: _LightVolumes
tooltips.text: Requires VRC Light Volumes 2.1.3+, installed via VCC alongside the shader.

tooltips.name: _LVPointShading
tooltips.text: How strongly Point Light Volumes are shaped by the surface normal. Only used when VRC Light Volumes 3.x or newer is installed - on 2.x the shader calls an overload that has no shading and this does nothing. 0 disables per-surface shading, 1 is the standard smooth gradient, higher is sharper. Leave at 1 unless you want a harder falloff: LV 3.x's own default when the argument is omitted is 3, which is what makes lighting snap between areas.

tooltips.name: _ProbeDirLight
tooltips.text: Shades the eye using a light direction recovered from the world's light probes. Most VRChat worlds have no realtime directional light, and without one the eye is lit by flat ambient and loses its roundness.

tooltips.name: _ProbeDirStrength
tooltips.text: How strongly the probe-derived light shapes the eye. It only applies where there is no strong realtime light, so raising it will not affect brightly lit worlds.

tooltips.name: _EmMode
tooltips.text: How the audio drives the glow. Pulse takes the band level directly. Sweep Up walks the band's history up the eye so the audio travels. Center Out Pulse rings outward from a point.

tooltips.name: _EmPulseScale
tooltips.text: Spacing of the rings in Center Out Pulse mode.

tooltips.name: _EmCenter
tooltips.text: The point the pulse radiates from, in UV space.

tooltips.name: _EmALEnable
tooltips.text: Turns AudioLink reactivity on for the eye's glow.

tooltips.name: _EmBand
tooltips.text: Which frequency band drives the glow.

tooltips.name: _EmAL
tooltips.text: How much the chosen band boosts brightness on top of the base emission.

tooltips.name: _EmHueOn
tooltips.text: Rotates the glow's hue with the audio.

tooltips.name: _EmVolBoost
tooltips.text: Scales the reaction by overall volume, so quiet passages react less.

tooltips.name: _EmVolAmt
tooltips.text: How strongly overall volume boosts the reaction.

tooltips.name: _EmMultBand
tooltips.text: A second band that scales the primary signal, so one frequency can gate another.

tooltips.name: _EmMultAmt
tooltips.text: How strongly the multiplier band scales the signal. 0 disables it.

tooltips.name: _EmAddBand
tooltips.text: A band added on top of the primary signal.

tooltips.name: _EmAddAmt
tooltips.text: How much the additive band contributes. 0 disables it.

tooltips.name: _EmLightBased
tooltips.text: Dims or lifts the glow depending on how lit the eye is.

tooltips.name: _EmMinEmiss
tooltips.text: Glow multiplier when the eye is in shadow.

tooltips.name: _EmMaxEmiss
tooltips.text: Glow multiplier when the eye is fully lit.

tooltips.name: _EmMinLight
tooltips.text: Lighting level treated as fully dark.

tooltips.name: _EmMaxLight
tooltips.text: Lighting level treated as fully lit.

tooltips.name: _EmBlink
tooltips.text: Pulses the glow on and off over time.

tooltips.name: _EmBlinkSpeed
tooltips.text: How fast the glow blinks.

tooltips.name: _EmBlinkMin
tooltips.text: How dim the bottom of each blink gets. 0 blinks fully off.

tooltips.name: _EmScan
tooltips.text: Sweeps a bright band across the glow, like a scanner.

tooltips.name: _EmScanMode
tooltips.text: Loop jumps back to the start each cycle. Ping Pong bounces back and forth.

tooltips.name: _EmScanSpeed
tooltips.text: How fast the band travels.

tooltips.name: _EmScanWidth
tooltips.text: Thickness of the moving band.

tooltips.name: _EmScanSoft
tooltips.text: How soft the band's edges are. 0 is a hard edge.

tooltips.name: _EmScanFloor
tooltips.text: How much the rest of the glow still shows outside the band. 0 shows only the band.

tooltips.name: _EmScanSpace
tooltips.text: Which space the band travels through. UV follows the texture unwrap. Object Space sweeps through the eye's own space, so a band can cross it on any axis and be matched to a sweep running across the body.

tooltips.name: _EmScanAxis
tooltips.text: Which way the band travels through the eye's own space. 0,1,0 sweeps upward, 1,0,0 across, 0,0,1 front to back. Values in between give diagonals.

tooltips.name: _EmScanExtent
tooltips.text: How far the sweep travels in metres. Match this across every material that should share the same wave.

tooltips.name: _EmScanStyle
tooltips.text: Shape of the sweep. Linear is a straight band travelling along the angle below. Radial rings outward from the centre, which suits an iris. Angular rotates around the centre like a clock hand.

tooltips.name: _EmScanAngle
tooltips.text: Direction the band travels in Linear, or the starting point of the rotation in Angular. 0 sweeps upward, 90 sweeps across.

tooltips.name: _EmScanCenter
tooltips.text: The point Radial and Angular sweeps revolve around, in UV space. Set it to the pupil for an iris effect.

tooltips.name: _EmScanOrigin
tooltips.text: Where the sweep begins, in metres along the chosen direction from the avatar's origin. Set every material on the avatar to the same start and length and a single band will cross all of them as one wave.

tooltips.name: _EmScanPhase
tooltips.text: Shifts where this material sits in the sweep cycle. Leave at 0 when several materials should move as one; nudge it to make a part lead or trail the rest.

tooltips.name: _ALMasterEnable
tooltips.text: Master switch for AudioLink on this material. Off silences every reactive effect at once, without touching each one's own toggle. It is a plain float, so it animates from a menu: use it to turn a whole avatar's reactivity on and off in one control.

tooltips.name: _ALEnvEnable
tooltips.text: Smooths AudioLink reactions: a fast rise on the beat with a tunable tail, so the eye pulses musically rather than flickering.

tooltips.name: _ALEnvRelease
tooltips.text: How long reactions take to fall after a beat. Low is snappy, high holds and glides. Match this to the main shader so an eye and the body decay together.
